X.note: Heavily weathered plaster, warm raking light and a rich cobbled street give real atmosphere and depth. The blown-out yellow patch on the left wall and the over-saturated orange and pink stains look procedural and too uniform. The crowd is tiny, stiff, faceless mannequins in flat blue and khaki, and they look like game assets. The small Union Jack, ship and distant hills read well.

Y.note: Cleaner and more believable architecture, with sensible stone cornices, plinths and pastel stucco, and soft even lighting. The surfaces are plain, flat and CG-clean, and the cobbles are barely readable. The left pink wall is flat and empty. The crowd is the same stiff blue and khaki mannequins, and the ground looks bluish and washed out. It reads as a sterile architectural render.

why: X has stronger lighting, depth and tactile aging that sell a lived-in 1943 Gibraltar street, while Y is cleaner but flat and sterile; both share the same toy-like crowd.
top_fix_for_weaker: Add weathering (plaster damage, grime streaks, stained stone), real directional sun with cast shadows, and visible cobble texture to Y. Replace the mannequin crowd with varied, properly modelled and animated figures, with period uniform textures and fewer flat blue ones.
anachronisms_seen: Modern-looking flat blue figure clothing (looks like modern work uniforms, not 1943 naval or military dress)
Pristine, uniform plaster and trim in Y that look newly built rather than wartime-worn
Very clean modern-looking dark metal balcony railings and shutters
